tasks.short: Design music therapy experiences around the client's goals

steps.what: Review the client's actual goals, capabilities, preferences and relevant treatment constraints
inputs: authorized existing client goals and treatment context

steps.what: Locate suitable existing music and activity resources and assess their musical characteristics
inputs: existing therapist-curated music and activity library
outputs: therapist-selected musical resources with relevant characteristics checked

steps.what: Design the actual experience using musical elements, participation demands and adaptations appropriate to the client
inputs: therapist-selected musical resources with relevant characteristics checked

steps.what: Write and check the experience instructions, chosen musical elements and planned adaptations
Save the checked experience instructions in the existing design document

tasks.design: Configure saved filters in {OTHER}, the existing therapist-curated music/activity library, for characteristics already recorded there. The therapist checks resources against actual goals from {OPS_SYSTEM}, designs the experience and records substantive instructions in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating existing suitable resources can require repeated library navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native library filters can reuse existing musical-characteristic metadata.
tasks.still_hard: Match musical elements and participation demands to this client's needs.
tasks.human_edge: Design a meaningful and clinically appropriate experience.

ambition.what: Reduce resource navigation without generated treatment design.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-5; library access, music-use permission and therapist consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: curated music libraries can filter existing resource characteristics; music therapists still select and adapt experiences to actual client goals.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the therapy record; OTHER is the existing curated music/activity library. Existing library authors provide metadata; no new tagging or automatic therapeutic classification is assumed. If metadata is absent, retain manual search.

Native filters first. This task owns the detailed musical experience instructions, not goal establishment or overall program customization. Existing goals are inputs, not re-authored here. No recording or generated music.
Shares are unmeasured provisional scenarios. Gross 2 minus 0.3 filter upkeep gives 1.7 net. Substantive experience design, instructions and 1% same-system save remain fully retained.
unknowns: Library metadata and actual navigation burden
research_questions: Can native filters reduce resource navigation while preserving therapist assessment of musical and clinical fit?

already_counted.description: Assess filtered resources against actual design requirements

approvals.approved_version: complete musical experience instructions checked at end of s4; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if metadata absent or existing search sufficient; cautious range below provisional 1.7% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Build rapport and discuss clients' progress and musical reactions

steps.what: Review actual prior session observations and agreed goals relevant to the client conversation
inputs: authorized actual session notes and client goals
outputs: therapist's source-checked context without inferred progress

steps.what: Communicate with the client to build rapport, acknowledge actual progress and reflect on their reactions to musical experiences
inputs: therapist's source-checked context without inferred progress
outputs: actual therapeutic conversation and client reactions understood

steps.what: Write and check the normal session note distinguishing client statements, observed reactions and therapist interpretation
inputs: actual therapeutic conversation and client reactions understood

steps.what: Save the checked session note in the same therapy record

tasks.design: Retain direct therapeutic communication and its normal note in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Native session headings and prior-note access already serve this scenario; no additional reduction is established for the actual client interaction or substantive note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rapport and reflection depend on the client's actual responses.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical record tools support context and notes but do not replace the relationship.
tasks.still_hard: Understand what a musical experience meant to this client.
tasks.human_edge: Listen, acknowledge and respond without imposing a progress narrative.

ambition.what: Keep therapeutic rapport and reflection with the therapist.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: therapeutic rapport and reflection require actual client communication; session documentation must distinguish reported and observed responses.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the existing therapy record. This is a documented clinical conversation scenario; source review, note authoring and save are split explicitly from the conversation, not omitted to declare zero.

Native prior-note views and session headings already available. No ambient recording or model-generated reflection is introduced. Any note shared with another session task must be counted once in synthesis.
Shares are unmeasured provisional scenarios. All work remains; gross and net zero. Same-system save is 1% fully retained, and note checking is ordinary authoring work.
unknowns: Actual note ownership and whether any duplicate entry exists outside the native record
research_questions: Observe the session note separately from conversation and identify any actual duplicate entry before estimating it.

already_counted.description: Write and check actual session observations and client statements

incremental.description: No new system or maintenance work

approvals.approved_version: complete session note checked at end of s3; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Native context access, substantive note and direct communication retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Customize music-therapy treatment programs for the specific setting and population

steps.what: Review the actual client population, setting constraints, established goals and overall care context
inputs: authorized actual client and setting information

steps.what: Choose appropriate program structure, musical participation demands, pacing and adaptations for the actual setting
Write and finish checking the customized treatment program with actual adaptations and existing client/episode identifiers
Save the checked customized program in the same therapy plan record

tasks.design: Configure program headings and existing episode fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The therapist determines and checks every setting-specific adaptation; the template does not choose a program from a diagnostic label or populate default clinical decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Written program customization may repeat layout and client/episode identifiers.
tasks.enabler_now: Native plan templates can supply nonclinical structure and existing identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Adapt participation and pacing to actual needs and setting constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the individual and practical care context beyond a population category.

ambition.what: Reduce repeated plan formatting without automatic treatment customization.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-5; clinical plan-owner consultation and record access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: music-therapy programs require setting-specific adaptation; clinical plan templates can supply headings and episode identifiers without selecting treatment.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the therapy plan record. Existing sources produce setting/context facts; therapist evaluates them in s1 and chooses actual adaptations in s2. No hidden structured clinical capture or diagnosis-to-program rule.

Native template first. This task owns program structure and setting-specific adaptations. Goals are inputs from goal establishment, and detailed musical experience instructions are another task; do not re-count their authoring or the same save in synthesis.
Shares are unmeasured provisional scenarios. Gross 3.9 minus 0.5 template upkeep gives 3.4 net. Same-system save remains fully retained at 1%; checking is part of ordinary program authoring.
unknowns: Current program format and whether program, goals and experience design share one physical record
research_questions: Which formatting is actually repeated, and how should shared plan authoring and save ownership be counted once?

already_counted.description: Author and check actual setting-specific program

incremental.description: Maintain program headings and identifier fields

approvals.approved_version: complete customized program checked at end of s3; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if native template already sufficient or formatting counted elsewhere; cautious range below provisional 3.4% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Establish client goals and objectives for music therapy

steps.what: Assess actual client needs, capabilities, interests and the overall treatment and coordination context
inputs: client's actual needs, capabilities and interests

steps.what: Discuss and establish appropriate client-specific goals and objectives considering actual treatment scope and duration
inputs: client's actual priorities and relevant care-team input
outputs: therapist-established goals and objectives with actual agreement and limitations

steps.what: Write and check the actual goals, observation criteria and review timing in the existing goal fields
inputs: therapist-established goals and objectives with actual agreement and limitations
outputs: complete checked music-therapy goals and objectives record

steps.what: Save the checked goals in the same therapy plan record
inputs: complete checked music-therapy goals and objectives record
outputs: saved actual music-therapy goals and objectives

tasks.design: Configure existing client and review-field headings in {OPS_SYSTEM} for goal recording. The therapist assesses, discusses and formulates the actual goals and checks the written objectives; no preset goal is selected from a disability or setting label.
tasks.previous_blocker: Goal documentation may repeat headings and client/episode fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Native goal fields can reuse these nonclinical details.
tasks.still_hard: Set meaningful and realistic objectives that reflect the client and coordinated treatment.
tasks.human_edge: Hear the client's priorities and negotiate appropriate goals.

ambition.what: Reduce small documentation setup while retaining goal establishment.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: therapy goals require client-specific assessment and discussion; native record fields can organize the resulting goals without choosing them.

assumptions: OPS_SYSTEM is the therapy plan record. Therapist produces actual assessed context in s1 and goals in s2; no structured preference form or inferred agreement is assumed.

Native headings first. This task owns goal content, not program customization or detailed musical experience design. If these share one care-plan record, synthesis must count actual overlapping authoring and the save once.

Shares are unmeasured provisional scenarios. Gross 1.2 minus 0.2 heading upkeep gives 1 net. All substantive goal formulation remains; 1% same-system save is fully retained and ordinary checking is inside authoring.
unknowns: Existing goal fields and actual overlap with treatment-plan authoring
research_questions: Is any goal-record setup repeated, and which task owns the shared plan save?

already_counted.description: Write and check actual client goals and review criteria

approvals.approved_version: complete actual goals and objectives checked at end of s3; edits void check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if native fields already sufficient or setup overlaps another task; cautious range below provisional 1% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

reach: Care teams contribute actual treatment context; therapists retain music-therapy goals, program choices and client communication.
skills_to_grow: Preserve client statements and observed reactions distinctly
Use curated music metadata without clinical inference
Resolve ownership of shared plan authoring and saves
role.ambitious_version: Improve resource access and reduce verified repeated plan fields while preserving individualized musical design, therapeutic rapport and client-led goals.
